hypothesis: Jerome's message ansatz (docs/JEROME_CALL_2026-09-25.md Q2/Q3/Q4): is a BP message of the form 'a Gaussian pushed through one transition of the true chain' -- what he called 'Gaussian plus the family of epsilon' -- exact when the innovation is that same family? Derived before measuring: NO. The recursion is L_{i+1} = dilate_rho(L_i * ell_i) conv p_eps, and (G conv p_eps) * N is not of the form (Gaussian conv p_eps), so the family is not closed. It IS exact in two limits: at site 1, where L_1 is the Gaussian prior pushed through one transition by construction, and as t grows and the likelihood flattens.
design: Forward messages of grid BP at (N_g = 801, A = 12), rho = 0.85, L = 32, 64 chains per cell, four innovation families (laplace, gaussian control, student, uniform) x the twelve frozen levels, read at sites (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 31). Each message is fitted by direct Nelder-Mead minimisation of KL(true || candidate) over the candidate's own parameters -- every family given its best shot rather than a moment match -- for three candidates: gaussian (2 params), gauss_through_transition (2 params; Jerome's ansatz, built with the recursion's OWN kernel matrix so the quadrature matches exactly), gauss_plus_laplace (4 params). Part `cumulants` reports standardised kappa_3..kappa_6 of the same messages against t and site, the representation-independent form of the question and the direct input to E23's truncation order.
predeclared_analysis: P1 gauss_through_transition divergence at site 1 sits at the numerical floor. P2 it GROWS with site index into the interior: the family is not a fixed point. P3 it is non-monotone in t. P4 a plain Gaussian is uniformly worse at small t and converges to it as t grows. P5 message excess kurtosis decays with t, setting E23's mode budget. The floor is MEASURED, not assumed: the Gaussian-innovation family is the control, where all three candidates contain the true message exactly, so its KL at the same (level, site, ansatz) is pure quadrature. A failure of P2 -- divergence flat in site index at the control level -- would mean the ansatz IS closed and the grid could be replaced by four numbers; that is the better outcome, which is why the prediction is recorded in advance.

seeds.confirmatory: deterministic per cell: rng_for('e22-shapes', family, level), 64 chains

status: REGISTERED 2026-09-25 and RUN on the laptop (48 cells, 4 workers). P1 and P2 confirmed for every family and every level; P3 FALSIFIED. Outputs under outputs/E22/ (shapes.csv, shapes_summary.csv, closure_verdict.csv, cumulants.csv); not yet frozen.
motivation: Jerome asked this three separate ways in one call and it had never been looked at: 'if you look at the messages mu_K, what do they look like?'; 'what if you take a Laplace ansatz for the messages in the BP -- is this exact when the innovation is exact? To me it's not immediate that they match'; 'I wonder if it's not Gaussian plus the family of epsilon'. It is the cheapest open question on the list and it decides two things at once: whether the real-space grid can be replaced by a handful of parameters, and how many modes a truncated representation needs at each level (E23).
development_note: The first implementation built the ansatz with a p_eps(u_i - u_j) lookup matrix applied to an already-dilated Gaussian, and measured 5.9e-8 nats at site 1 where the ansatz is analytically exact. That residual was the gap between two discretisations of the same convolution -- BP evaluates p_eps at the off-grid points u_i - rho u_j with the dilation folded into the kernel, a grid lookup cannot -- and reported as-is it would have looked like a small failure of the ansatz rather than a failure of the comparison. Rebuilding the candidate on the recursion's own kernel matrix takes the same site-1 fit to 3.8e-17, which is what makes P1 a usable control.
code_change: Adds `return_messages=True` to `markov_score.bp_grid.grid_bp`, exposing the normalised forward and backward messages. The alternative was a second implementation of the same sweep inside an experiment, which the module docstring and backend.py both argue against. Default behaviour is unchanged (fields default to None); 57 BP/EM/oracle tests pass unchanged.

outcome.Q3: Jerome's conjecture is very nearly right. The two-parameter 'Gaussian pushed through one transition' family beats a plain Gaussian by 1600x (Laplace) and 16000x (Student-t) at t=0.05, and beats the FOUR-parameter Gaussian+Laplace mixture by 50x. The right two-parameter family beats a wrong four-parameter family by fifty: structure beats capacity.
outcome.Q2: Not exact. P1 holds everywhere -- site-1 KL is 2.5e-15 to 3.1e-14, machine precision, as derived, since L_1 is the Gaussian prior pushed through exactly one transition. P2 holds everywhere -- the divergence grows by ~10^10 into the chain interior (site 31), for all four families and all twelve levels. The family is not a fixed point of the recursion.
outcome.Q4: Exact closure is Gaussian-only (site 1 vs site 31 is the demonstration). Projected closure is available for any family at a price now measured rather than asserted: 1e-5 to 1e-3 nats per message for the best two-parameter family.
outcome.P3_falsified: Predicted the ansatz error would be SMALLEST at large t, because the likelihood flattens and the product step stops acting. Measured the opposite: for Laplace and Student the error grows monotonically with t (2.2e-5 -> 7.7e-4; 1.8e-6 -> 8.8e-4); only uniform is non-monotone. The prediction had the large-t limit backwards. With the likelihood flat the recursion is a pure repeated convolution, which drives the message to the chain's STATIONARY law -- an infinite convolution, maximally far from 'one Gaussian through one transition'. At small t the likelihood is sharp, L_i*ell_i is nearly a point mass, and the next message is nearly p_eps shifted, which is exactly in the family. The ansatz is best where the data is most informative.
outcome.mode_budget_for_E23: Odd cumulants are negligible (1e-3..1e-2; symmetric innovations), so a truncation can carry even orders only. Order 4 is NOT enough: |kappa_6| runs 1 to 228 and is never small, so the Gaussian-plus-kappa_4 rung that e16_edgeworth_oracle builds will miss a large term; E23 must reach order 6 at least, more for heavy tails. |kappa_4| decays with t but PLATEAUS (2.12 -> 0.48 for Laplace) because the message tends to the stationary law rather than to a Gaussian, so a t-adaptive truncation saves less than one might hope.
